page_title: High Agency in 30 Minutes – George Mack

summary.title: High Agency in 30 Minutes – George Mack
summary.one_liner: High agency is a mindset of solving problems by first checking whether they defy physics, then acting on them, and it can be built by escaping common "low agency" traps.
takeaways: High agency rests on three skills together: clear thinking, bias to action, and disagreeability.
A problem that does not defy the laws of physics is treated as solvable, regardless of what others say.
Low agency traps (such as the vague trap) keep people stuck; the essay proposes escape routes like writing problems down in simple words.
Heroes are human: don't put authorities on pedestals, and verify claims from first principles rather than accepting them passively.
summary.summary: This long essay by George Mack argues that high agency, the tendency to shape the future through action rather than accept it, is the most important idea of the 21st century. It defines high agency through examples such as a hypothetical call from a jail cell, historical cases like Roulette hacking by Shannon and Thorp, and the Wright brothers, and lists traits for spotting it. The essay presents five "software" beliefs (no unsolvable problem, no way, no adults, no normal, only now) and five low agency traps, each with an escape route. It is written in an informal, anecdote-driven style and is listed as a roughly 30-minute read.
